Tests/Linq/OrmBattle/OrmBattleTests.cs::.quote: gate: 'Bad database data' - refuted at OrmBattleTests.cs:57
Tests/Linq/OrmBattle/OrmBattleTests.cs::.note: The gate's claim is false. `Customers ??= db.Customer.ToList()` (OrmBattleTests.cs:57) loads the in-memory reference from the very database the test compares against, so the two sides hold identical data by construction and no dataset difference is possible. What differs is ordering: `result` is ordered by SQLite's `ORDER BY City` under BINARY collation, `expected` by .NET's culture-aware string comparison, and the test asserts SequenceEqual across the two. Addressing it means fixing the comparison (ordinal comparer, or ordering both sides in the CLR), not the data - which is a change to an OrmBattle benchmark test's semantics and therefore the user's call.

Tests/Linq/Linq/JoinTests.cs::SqlLinqCro.quote: gate said "Cross-join doesn't work in Sybase" - refuted by measurement
Tests/Linq/Linq/JoinTests.cs::SqlLinqCro.sweptOn: 2026-09-08 local, net10.0, Sybase.Managed (the native Sybase provider is netfx-only, so it has no case here)
Tests/Linq/Linq/JoinTests.cs::SqlLinqCro.note: The assert is correct: 7 parents x 10 children is 70 rows and Sybase returns 10. The cause is not the cross join. A playground probe on Sybase.Managed with SQLite.MS as control measured the same query with Take on both sides (10 vs 70), neither side (119 vs 119), left only (10 vs 119) and right only (10 vs 70): every arm carrying a Take caps at exactly 10, so ASE applies a derived table's TOP to the outer result. linq2db already sets IsSubQueryTakeSupported and IsCorrelatedSubQueryTakeSupported false for Sybase but leaves IsDerivedTableTakeSupported at the base default of true; flipping it was probed and is not a fix - the query then fails to translate at all, because Sybase has no window functions to emulate the paging with. Product defect, no tracker entry; worth its own issue. Filed as #5895 (2026-09-08).

Tests/Linq/Update/MergeTests.Operations..quote: gate said "Cross-join doesn't work in Sybase. Also see SqlLinqCrossJoinSubQuery test" - refuted by measurement

Tests/Linq/Update/MergeTests.Operations..note: The assert is correct: 2 left x 2 right is 4 source rows and the Merge reports 2 affected. Tests/Linq/Linq/WhereTests.cs::StringInt.observed: Sybase renders a null MiddleName's `?? ""` slot as " ", so FullName reads "( + )" on the CLR and "(  +  )" from the database
Tests/Linq/Linq/WhereTests.cs::StringInt.note: Gate removed in favour of a provider-specific expectation: the query is unchanged and, on Sybase, the expected rows are rebuilt over a Person sequence whose null MiddleName already reads as " ". MiddleName is Person's only nullable member, so it is the only place a `?? ""` fires. A second ASE fact forced that shape: hoisting the fallback into a variable makes it a parameter, linq2db sizes a string parameter from its value, and ASE types COALESCE by the parameter's declared length - "Ko" came back as "K". Both fallbacks therefore stay literals. Verified green on Sybase.Managed plus SQLite.MS and SQLite.Classic as controls.

Tests/Linq/UserTests/Issue2832Tests.cs::.note: The gate was wrong about its own symptom. The test only builds SQL and counts accessible sources; nothing runs, so no conversion error can arise and #5590 (the YDB "could not be converted to SQL" issue) does not apply. The named cause is sound - YDB sets IsSupportedSimpleCorrelatedSubqueries false, so the optimizer cannot collapse the subqueries the way the other providers do. Resolved as a provider-specific assert on the user's call: the bound is 5 on YDB and 2 elsewhere. Verified green on YDB direct and remote.

Tests/Linq/Linq/WindowFunctionsTests.Rat.quote: gate cited #5663 "DB2: DECFLOAT special values (Infinity/NaN) fail column mapping to decimal" - closed, and about a decimal column
Tests/Linq/Linq/WindowFunctionsTests.Rat.note: The gate said the reader cannot map the special value. It maps it fine: the result materialises as double INF / -INF and the assertion fails because the test wants null. DB2 has a native RATIO_TO_REPORT, so linq2db emits it directly and it never reaches the NULLIF emulation that makes a zero partition total yield NULL elsewhere. Filed as #5897 and re-attributed. Verified Inconclusive on DB2 direct and remote.
Tests/Linq/Linq/WindowFunctionsTests.Rat.observed: Shouldly.ShouldAssertException : result should satisfy the condition (r.RatioToReport == null) but [{ Id = 1, RatioToReport = INF }, { Id = 2, RatioToReport = -INF }] do not

Tests/Linq/Linq/MathFunctionTests.cs::Ro.quote: gate: "Wrong DB2 implementation" - the only gate this session whose stated cause survived measurement
Tests/Linq/Linq/MathFunctionTests.cs::Ro.note: Probed against the live server because linq2db emits a banker's-rounding CASE rather than a plain ROUND, so the emulation was the obvious suspect. It is exonerated: for 6.6, 9.6 and 1.1 the midpoint branch is never taken, so the CASE reduces to plain ROUND - and ROUND(CAST(6.6 AS Float), 5) returns 6.6000000000000005 on its own, one ulp above the nearest double to 6.6. DB2's ROUND on a Float is simply not exact. Nothing to fix on our side and not worth filing against IBM, so a no-issue: marker. The user chose activeissue over a tolerance-based provider-specific assert.

Tests/Linq/Linq/ConcatUnionTests.cs::Iss.quote: driver, not server: the message text is the CLI driver's stand-in for one it could not encode
Tests/Linq/Linq/ConcatUnionTests.cs::Iss.note: Quarantined for CI under A-15, same root cause as the eight Informix sites in A-13: this workstation runs with the UTF-8 ACP (65001) and the IBM CLI driver cannot convert it to UTF-16, so it fails while rendering the server's own error text.
